cleanIntro: Ruger publishes no disassembly for the SP101 — it states the mechanism is lubricated without taking anything apart. This guide is the cleaning it does document.

steps.title: Swing the cylinder out and empty it
steps.action: Open the cylinder and confirm every chamber is empty, by eye and by finger.
steps.prose: Five chambers on this revolver. Check all five.
steps.quote: To clean the revolver after firing, swing the cylinder out and clean the barrel from the muzzle
steps.cite: Ruger SP101 Instruction Manual — PM053 — Care and Cleaning, p.15

steps.title: Nothing comes apart — and that is the instruction
steps.action: There is no field strip to perform. Ruger states the SP101 mechanism can be lubricated without disassembly.
steps.prose: A few drops of light firearm oil applied periodically about the frame openings work their way into the mechanism. That is the whole internal maintenance the manual describes.
steps.quote: The internal mechanism of the SP101
steps.cite: Ruger SP101 Instruction Manual — PM053 — Care and Cleaning, p.15

deepAbsentReason: The SP101 manual documents no disassembly at all — it states the internal mechanism can be lubricated without disassembly (Care and Cleaning, p.15). With no field strip published there is nothing "past" it, so this listing has NO deep clean.

cleaning.name: BORE
tasks: Swing the cylinder out and clean the barrel from the muzzle with a solvent-coated patch, several passes
Push a correctly sized bronze wire brush the full length of the bore several times
Swab with a solvent patch again, then wipe the rod and swab with dry patches until clean
Examine the bore to be sure no fouling remains

cleaning.name: CHAMBERS
tasks: Repeat the bore procedure for each of the five chambers

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR & MECHANISM
tasks: Apply a few drops of light firearm oil periodically about the various frame openings and let it work into the mechanism
Wipe the exterior, bore and chambers, then wipe with an oily cloth if the revolver is going into storage

fncheck: With the revolver confirmed empty, check the cylinder swings out and indexes freely, and dry fire pointed in a safe direction.
